clue.text: Prefer to attack

definitions.meaning: to favour or choose one thing over another
to set upon someone, physically or verbally

explanation.surface: Someone would rather launch an assault than hold back.
explanation.definitionFit: To go for something can mean liking it best, and to go for someone means lunging at them.

clue.text: Faster way to gun down the enemy

indicators.note: a different way of arranging the letters of the word before it, so they are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A quicker method of shooting opposing soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' signals a rearrangement of the six letters of FASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack ground troops with machine-gun fire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: Is male in the group to be ousted?

indicators.note: the words before go inside the word for group that follows

parts.note: a band is a group of people or musicians
taken as written
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the only man in the team is about to be kicked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is male' reads like a question about a man, but the two words are simply letters placed inside the group word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being banished means being expelled or sent away, which is what ousted describes.

clue.text: Tie-breaker leads to dramatic cancellation

definitions.meaning: an extra match held to settle a drawn contest
a play called off, a theatre piece that does not go ahead

explanation.surface: A deciding match ends with a theatrical show being scrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciding extra game is the sporting sense; a stage show called off reads the phrase literally.

clue.text: Rising journalist stopped being late

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ED is the usual abbreviation for an editor, a senior journalist
ceased means stopped or came to an end

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming reporter has quit being tardy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns ED into DE in this down entry. 'late' means dead here, not tardy.
explanation.definitionFit: Late, as in 'the late king', means having died recently, the same as deceased.

clue.text: Gathering to study the circuit

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
a course is a racing circuit or track

explanation.surface: A meeting called to examine the racetrack.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a crowd or assembly of people brought together.

clue.text: Serving man's error corrected by podiatrist

definitions.text: Serving man's error corrected by podiatrist

parts.words: Serving man's error corrected by podiatrist
parts.note: a tennis server's mistake of stepping over the baseline, read as a flaw in the feet that a foot doctor might treat

explanation.surface: A waiter's mistake is put right by a chiropodist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serving man' suggests a waiter or servant, but it is a tennis player serving.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis this is a service fault for stepping on or over the baseline, and a podiatrist treats feet.

clue.text: Board has to succeed

definitions.meaning: to climb aboard a bus, train or ship
to make progress or prosper in life

explanation.surface: A company's directors must prosper.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on a train is boarding it, and getting on in the world means doing well.

clue.text: Vessel in the brewery

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A container found at a beer-making plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug or pitcher, a kind of vessel for liquid.

clue.text: My tailor makes distinction between right and wrong

indicators.note: the letters of the two words before are made into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tailor with a strong sense of ethics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' signals rearranging the letters of MY TAILOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethics concerns the principles of good and bad conduct, which is what distinguishing right from wrong means.

clue.text: Tool used to construct St Clement Danes, say

parts.note: Sir Christopher Wren was the architect who rebuilt St Clement Danes after the Great Fire
St Clement Danes is a London church, and CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: An implement employed in building a famous London church.
explanation.walkthrough: St Clement Danes is a London church on the Strand, so it is a WREN CH, a Wren church.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrench is a spanner, a hand tool for gripping and turning nuts.

clue.text: Prepared to take Henry as Abel's replacement

parts.note: set means ready or prepared
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Ready to bring in a man called Henry as a substitute for Abel.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Eve names her third son as God's replacement for Abel, who was killed by Cain.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Eve says God has given her another son in place of the murdered Abel.

clue.text: Pays up to have some cutlery displayed

parts.note: forks are items of cutlery
out means on show, displayed

explanation.surface: Someone settles a bill so as to lay out the silverware.
explanation.definitionFit: To fork out is to hand over money, often reluctantly.

clue.text: Mechanical failure calls for detailed analysis

definitions.meaning: a car or machine ceasing to work
an itemised account splitting figures into parts

explanation.surface: An engine fault demands a careful investigation.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle failing on the road is one sense; an itemised split of costs or data is the other.

clue.text: He's so boring I'm bored to bits

definitions.note: a person described as tedious; the answer names such a dull person or remark

indicators.note: the words before are broken into pieces and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone is so dull it is driving the speaker mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bits' signals rearranging the letters of I'M BORED.
explanation.definitionFit: A bromide is a trite remark or a tiresome person, from the sedative drug's dulling effect.

clue.text: Apply cosmetics ingratiate oneself

definitions.meaning: to try to win favour or flirt with someone

explanation.surface: Putting on make-up to curry favour.
explanation.definitionFit: Making up to someone can mean painting their face or sucking up to them.

clue.text: Watched boss return remains of the wood

parts.note: saw is the past tense of see, meaning watched

indicators.note: read as re-turn, a turning around again, so the letters of the boss word are reordered

parts.note: a stud is a raised boss or knob on a surface

explanation.surface: Seeing the manager come back to what is left of a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' rearranges STUD into DUST; a plain reversal would give DUTS, so the setter's device is loose here.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawdust is the fine powder left over when timber is cut.

clue.text: Dislike a biblical translation

parts.note: a version is a translation of the Bible, such as the Authorised Version

explanation.surface: Someone disapproves of a particular rendering of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong distaste for something.

clue.text: Make sweets with it? Nonsense!

definitions.meaning: a garden plant whose stalks are stewed into puddings and also flavour boiled sweets
an exclamation of disbelief, or the meaningless murmur actors make in crowd scenes

explanation.surface: A suggestion of a confectionery ingredient is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhubarb and custard are classic British boiled sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: The stalky plant is used in desserts and sweets, and the word is slang for drivel.

clue.text: Support corporal punishment, despite adverse reaction

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a lash is a stroke of the whip, a physical punishment

explanation.surface: Endorsing physical chastisement in spite of a hostile response.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlash is a strong negative public response to an event or change.

clue.text: Self-starter for a motor

definitions.meaning: the prefix that begins words meaning self, as in autobiography

explanation.surface: An electric ignition device for a car engine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek-derived prefix means self, and the short form of automobile means a car.

clue.text: Leisure facility

explanation.surface: A recreation centre or sports amenity.
explanation.definitionFit: A life of ease is one of relaxation, and doing something with ease means doing it with effortless skill.

clue.text: Guard the southern gate

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south or southern
an entry is a way in, such as a gate

explanation.surface: Protect the entrance on the south side.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier posted to keep watch.

clue.text: Old sultan was a very large fellow

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
a man is a fellow or chap

explanation.surface: A former ruler was an enormous chap.
explanation.walkthrough: Osman I founded the Ottoman Empire, which takes its name from him.
explanation.definitionFit: Osman was the first ruler of the Ottoman dynasty around 1300.

clue.text: Now scarcely needs to make modifications

parts.note: AD, anno domini, denotes the present era, so now
just means barely or scarcely

explanation.surface: At present it hardly needs any changes.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust is to alter something slightly to get it right.

clue.text: Elizabeth retains us in a regular job

indicators.note: keeps hold of the words that follow inside the name before

parts.note: Bess is a familiar form of Elizabeth
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman named Elizabeth keeps us on in steady employment.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's business is their occupation or line of work.

clue.text: Taunts the simple-minded

explanation.surface: Mocks people who are not very bright.
explanation.definitionFit: To twit someone is to tease them, and twits are fools.

clue.text: Check manuscript to get evidence stated in court

parts.note: proof is evidence that establishes a fact
a statement or charge is read out in court

explanation.surface: Review a document to obtain testimony given before a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: To proofread is to examine a text for errors before publication.
